**Composition of Oils/Fats:**
Oils and fats are chemically **triglycerides** (esters of glycerol with three fatty acid molecules). 
$$\text{Fatty Acids} + \text{Glycerol} \rightleftharpoons \text{Triglycerides} + \text{Water}$$

**Difference in Melting Point and Vapour Pressure:**
- **Melting Point:** Depends on saturation and chain length. Saturated fats (tightly packed straight chains) have higher melting points. Unsaturated fats (kinked chains due to double bonds) have lower melting points.
- **Vapour Pressure:** Both oils and fats have extremely low vapour pressures at room temperature because of their high molecular weights.

**Why Coconut Oil/Ghee are solid while vegetable oils are liquid:**
- **Ghee and Coconut oil** contain a high percentage of **saturated fatty acids** (e.g., lauric acid in coconut oil, butyric/palmitic acid in ghee), allowing molecules to pack closely and remain solid at room temperature.
- **Vegetable oils** (like soybean or sunflower oil) contain a high percentage of **unsaturated fatty acids** (oleic and linoleic acids) with cis-double bonds that prevent tight packing, keeping them liquid at room temperature.
